correctness.rationale: A structural 21-edge/7-colour/3-regularity argument forces every optimum to partition vertices into one nonincident point-line pair per colour. Two independent finite enumerations check all 5040 line-to-point bijections and all 135135 unordered vertex pairings, both returning exactly 8. The first also enumerates all 168 Fano collineations and computes a transitive orbit of size 8, hence stabilizer 21. Recorded programs and outputs replay exactly; no infinite claim.

originality.rationale: The 2023 Banff-design theorem proves existence of a seven-colour harmonious colouring and hence the known optimum, but provides no enumeration or group orbit of all optimal assignments. The 2024 nesting paper supplies an explicit order-seven construction and an equivalence, not the full count. The 2012 forest theorem has a distinct domain. Accessible internal historical claims and published research records gave no same or stronger complete Fano enumeration. The exact eight, 40,320 named colourings and 21-stabiliser conclusions remain not implied by the identified published statements; unindexed older nestings tables are a residual originality risk.
residual_risks: Classical or unpublished small-order nestings enumeration could already state the eight solutions and one-orbit property; original 1985 nesting article not inspected in full.
Search rankings cannot certify worldwide uniqueness; unpublished tables or alternate exact-colouring terminology may contain overlap.

value.rationale: Fano-plane nestings are a natural and explicitly studied extremal design construction. Existence of a harmonious seven-colouring was known, but does not determine how many optimum assignments exist or whether inequivalent nestings occur. The complete eight-solution census, full 40320 named-colouring count, and single 168-collineation orbit settle the natural entire optimum configuration space for this base case, a useful benchmark for larger Banff-design classifications; not an arbitrary induced graph or subset slice.
